title: Neutrino and Gravitational-Wave Detectors
welcome_lead: Look at the universe with something other than light.
final_note: Multi-messenger astronomy is now a reality.

concepts.def: Nearly massless, weakly interacting elementary particle.
50,000-tonne water Cherenkov neutrino detector in Japan.
Cubic-kilometre neutrino detector buried in Antarctic ice.
Light emitted when charged particles exceed light speed in a medium.
Laser interferometer that detects gravitational waves.
Combining photons, neutrinos and gravitational waves.

walkthroughs.body_html: Super-Kamiokande (1996) uses 50,000 tonnes of pure water; IceCube (2010) uses a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice. Both detect Cherenkov light from charged particles produced when neutrinos interact.
LIGO's two 4 km arms compare laser path lengths. A passing wave stretches and squeezes spacetime by less than one-ten-thousandth of a proton's width — and they detect it.
The neutron star merger GW170817 was seen in gravitational waves, gamma rays, optical and radio — the first true multi-messenger event, confirming that mergers make heavy elements like gold.
